trait.name: Tidebound
entries: The hand is strongest in the water. While the hand is in, on, or above water, it has Advantage on attack rolls. While it is over dry land, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: Something Has Your Ankle
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the hand hits a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it deals an extra 1 ({@damage 1d2}) Bludgeoning damage.
Stand on dry rock: on dry ground the hand's Speed is halved, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls, and it can't grip an ankle it can't reach through water.

action.name: Ankle Grip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is in water, it also has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). The hand can grapple only one creature at a time.

bonus.name: Out of the Sand (1/Day)
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11}, one creature in water that the hand can see within 10 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Underleaf
entries: While the rootlisten is within 5 feet of a tree, undergrowth, or its own roots, it has Half Cover (a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws) and moves through those spaces without spending extra movement. Burning or clearing the growth around it, or drawing it into open ground, takes this away.

trait.name: It Hears You Plan
entries: The rootlisten has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. It can't impose the Frightened condition on a creature that hasn't spoken aloud or cast a spell with a Verbal component since the end of the rootlisten's last turn.
The rootlisten can't impose the Frightened condition on a creature that hasn't spoken aloud or cast a spell with a Verbal component since the end of the rootlisten's last turn.

action.name: Root Needle
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Whisper It Back
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11}, one creature the rootlisten can see within 30 feet that has spoken aloud since the end of the rootlisten's last turn, repeating that creature's own words. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Catch the Whisper
entries: Trigger: A creature within 10 feet of the rootlisten speaks aloud or casts a spell with a Verbal component. Response: The rootlisten moves up to 10 feet toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Tidebound
entries: The netmouth is strongest in the water. While the netmouth is in, on, or above water, it has Advantage on attack rolls. While it is over dry land, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: It Was Not Dead
entries: While a creature the netmouth can see within 30 feet has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, the netmouth has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. If the netmouth takes Fire damage, this Resistance doesn't apply until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Lies in the Catch
entries: The netmouth can occupy another creature's space. While it hasn't moved or attacked since the end of its last turn, it looks like an ordinary heap of net and hooks, and a creature must take the Search action and succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom (Perception) check to tell the difference.

action.name: Hooked Gape
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Close the Mesh
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 11}, one creature in the netmouth's space. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. The netmouth can't move while it restrains a creature this way, and a creature within 5 feet can take an action to cut the mesh, ending the condition.

bonus.name: Something in the Net Moved
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11}, one creature the netmouth can see within 10 feet that has touched it or shares its space. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Deepsign
entries: The knocker reads the rock rather than the air. It has Tremorsense 60 feet. While a creature within 30 feet of it carries an uncovered light source that sheds Bright Light, the knocker has Disadvantage on attack rolls and can't take a Bonus Action. A covered lantern doesn't count; an open flame does.

trait.name: Knocks Twice for the Frightened
entries: Immediately after it takes the Attack action, the knocker can make one extra attack against a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Fire damage.

trait.name: Melted Joints
entries: While the knocker has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, its AC is reduced by 2.

action.name: Hot Knuckle
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Fire damage.

action.name: Soot Door (1/Day)
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 11}, each creature in a 10-foot Cone. {@actSaveFail} 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: The Door Has Sealed
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11}, one creature the knocker can see within 30 feet that can hear it. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Tidebound
entries: The caller is strongest in the water. While the caller is in, on, or above water, it has Advantage on attack rolls. While it is over dry land, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: It Knows Your Name
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the caller hits a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it deals an extra 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Necrotic damage. The caller can't impose the Frightened condition on a creature that hasn't spoken aloud within 60 feet of it since the end of the caller's last turn.

trait.name: Will Not Be Turned Away
entries: The caller has Advantage on saving throws against effects that would move it, push it, or turn it away, and it can't be forced across a threshold it has been invited through.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The caller makes two Remembered Hand attacks.

action.name: Remembered Hand
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Admission {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 12}, one creature the caller can see within 5 feet. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Necrotic damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 12}). While Grappled this way the target can't speak, though it breathes normally and can still use abilities with no verbal component. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: Calls You by Name
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 12}, one creature the caller can see within 60 feet that has spoken aloud since the end of the caller's last turn. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Tidebound
entries: The shorewaiter is strongest in the water. While the shorewaiter is in, on, or above water, it has Advantage on attack rolls. While it is over dry land, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: No One Should Wait Alone
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the shorewaiter hits a creature that has no conscious ally within 30 feet of it, that creature takes an extra 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Psychic damage, and the shorewaiter can then move up to 20 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: It Wants the Ones Who Wait
entries: The shorewaiter doesn't willingly attack a creature that hasn't struck it, taken something from its shore, or tried to lead a waiting person away from the water. It fights drowned callers and other coast monsters for the same people, and a party that stands aside may watch it do so.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The shorewaiter makes two Saltwood Reach attacks.

action.name: Saltwood Reach
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 10 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Make Room
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 12}, one Large or smaller creature the shorewaiter can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target is pushed up to 20 feet directly away from the nearest creature allied with it, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Reach for the Boat
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 12}, one Large or smaller creature the shorewaiter can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The shorewaiter pulls the target up to 30 feet directly toward itself along an unobstructed path, ending in an unoccupied space. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

reaction.name: Turn Seaward
entries: Trigger: A creature the shorewaiter can see ends its turn with no conscious ally within 30 feet of it. Response: The shorewaiter moves up to its Speed toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Anchored
entries: A high funeral chair of black oak, its seat worn pale and a place laid at it that nobody fills, stands in the seat's space and is part of its body. It has AC 12, 15 Hit Points, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and it can't move on its own. A creature can attack it, or take an action within 5 feet of it to cover it with an opaque cloth. While it is destroyed or covered, Keeps a Place for the Wounded does nothing, and the seat can take an action to uncover it. Destroying it deals no damage to the seat.

trait.name: Keeps a Place for the Wounded
entries: At the start of each of its turns, the seat regains 4 Hit Points if it can see, within 60 feet, a creature that has fewer than half its Hit Points remaining or a creature within 10 feet of a corpse. It regains these Hit Points once per turn no matter how many such creatures it sees, and not at all while it has the Incapacitated condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The seat makes two Empty Place attacks.

action.name: Empty Place
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5}, range 60 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Closed Vigil {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}, one creature the seat can see within 30 feet that can see the chair. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: Sit With Us
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, one creature the seat has damaged this turn and can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn, and also the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for that duration if it has fewer than half its Hit Points remaining. A creature within 5 feet of the target can take an action to end one of these conditions.

reaction.name: Pull Up a Chair
entries: Trigger: A creature the seat can see within 10 feet regains Hit Points. Response: The seat moves up to 10 feet toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This prevents no healing.

trait.name: Tidebound
entries: The shepherd is strongest in the water. While the shepherd is in, on, or above water, it has Advantage on attack rolls. While it is over dry land, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: Herding Fog
entries: A 20-foot Emanation of cold fog surrounds the shepherd, and that area is Lightly Obscured. Bright Light suppresses the fog within a 10-foot radius of the light, and an audible struck bell suppresses it within 30 feet of the bell until the end of the striker's next turn. The fog doesn't block Total Cover, hinder breathing, or let the shepherd see through walls.

trait.name: The Bell That Isn't There
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the shepherd hits a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it deals an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage. The shepherd can't impose the Frightened condition on a creature that is in Bright Light.

trait.name: Wind Scattered
entries: If the shepherd takes Thunder damage, its Fly Speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The shepherd makes two Cold Bell attacks.

action.name: Cold Bell
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 15 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Cold damage.

action.name: Borrowed Bell {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Cold damage, and the target has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: A Shape in the Haar
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, one creature the shepherd can see within 30 feet that is Lightly or Heavily Obscured. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Deepsign
entries: The redmeasure reads the rock rather than the air. It has Tremorsense 60 feet. While a creature within 30 feet of it carries an uncovered light source that sheds Bright Light, the redmeasure has Disadvantage on attack rolls and can't take a Bonus Action. A covered lantern doesn't count; an open flame does.

trait.name: Tally of Injuries
entries: The redmeasure keeps a count of who struck it. When it hits a creature that has damaged it since the end of its last turn, that creature takes an extra 1d6 Bludgeoning damage for each creature that has damaged the redmeasure since then, to a maximum of 10 ({@damage 3d6}). Striking it with one character instead of four keeps the tally short.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The redmeasure makes two Iron Measure attacks.

action.name: Iron Measure
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Broken Tally {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 15-foot Cube within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: Reads the Ledger Aloud
entries: The redmeasure names one creature it can see within 60 feet that has damaged it since the end of its last turn. Until the end of its next turn, it has Advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

reaction.name: Count the Injury
entries: Trigger: A creature the redmeasure can see damages it. Response: The redmeasure moves up to 15 feet toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Crowded Ground
entries: The envier is made of neighbors and is strongest where they stand close. It has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that has another creature within 5 feet of it, and Disadvantage on attack rolls against a creature that has no other creature within 15 feet of it.

trait.name: Envies the Untouched
entries: While the envier can see a creature within 60 feet that has taken no damage since the start of the envier's last turn, it has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Once everyone it can see has been hurt, there is nothing left for it to want, and the Resistance ends.

trait.name: Soft Corners
entries: The envier can move through a space as narrow as 1 foot without squeezing. It can't do so while it has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The envier makes two Window Spill attacks.

action.name: Window Spill
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 10 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 4d6 + 3}) Acid damage.

action.name: The Better Room
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15}, one creature the envier can see within 60 feet. A warm lit room shows in the lead-framed window at the envier's center, and in it the target's own life going better. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn and can't willingly move farther from the window during that time. The condition doesn't compel the target to attack anyone or hand over anything.

bonus.name: That Should Be Mine
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature the envier can see within 60 feet that has taken no damage since the start of the envier's last turn. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to break the hardened acid, ending the condition.

trait.name: Anchored
entries: A split fiddle, strapped against its exposed ribs and playing on its own, stands in the merry's space and is part of its body. It has AC 13, 25 Hit Points, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and it can't move on its own. A creature can attack it, or take an action within 5 feet of it to cover it with an opaque cloth. While it is destroyed or covered, Dances on What's Left does nothing, and the merry can take an action to uncover it. Destroying it deals no damage to the merry.

trait.name: Dances on What's Left
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the merry hits a creature that has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and can hear the fiddle, it deals an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Slashing damage. A creature can stand up normally, and a creature that covers both ears with an action can't hear the fiddle until it frees a hand.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The merry makes two Dancer Talon attacks.

action.name: Dancer Talon
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 3d8 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Splintered Caper {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the merry. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Slashing damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: One More Reel
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature the merry can see within 30 feet that can hear the fiddle. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

reaction.name: The Laugh Catches
entries: Trigger: A creature the merry can see within 30 feet stands up from Prone. Response: The merry moves up to 20 feet toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks. It can't use this reaction while it has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Underleaf
entries: While the bellwound is within 5 feet of a tree, undergrowth, or its own roots, it has Half Cover (a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws) and moves through those spaces without spending extra movement. Burning or clearing the growth around it, or drawing it into open ground, takes this away.

trait.name: Tolls for the Wounded
entries: At the start of each of its turns, the bellwound regains 9 Hit Points if it can see, within 60 feet, a creature that has fewer than half its Hit Points remaining or a creature within 10 feet of a corpse. It regains these Hit Points once per turn no matter how many such creatures it sees, and not at all while it has the Incapacitated condition. Healing the wounded above half their Hit Points shuts this off.

trait.name: Sightless Mourning
entries: A creature that has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} or {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition has Disadvantage on saving throws against the bellwound's Bonus Actions. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to wipe a target's eyes or ring a handbell by its ear, ending one such condition the bellwound caused.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bellwound makes two Root Toll attacks.

action.name: Root Toll
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 15 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Mourning Pollen {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Poison damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: The Unheard Bell
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, one creature the bellwound has damaged this turn and can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn, and also the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for that duration if it has fewer than half its Hit Points remaining.

trait.name: Deepsign
entries: The duchess reads the rock rather than the air. It has Tremorsense 60 feet. While a creature within 30 feet of it carries an uncovered light source that sheds Bright Light, the duchess has Disadvantage on attack rolls and can't take a Bonus Action. A covered lantern doesn't count; an open flame does.

trait.name: Envies the Untouched
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the duchess hits a creature that has taken no damage since the start of the duchess's last turn, it deals an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Piercing damage. Once a creature has been hurt, the duchess stops wanting what it has.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The duchess makes two Claimed Splinter attacks.

action.name: Claimed Splinter
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft. {@h}21 ({@damage 5d6 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Close the Seam {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, one creature on a stone surface the duchess can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Piercing damage, and the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to break the ore cage, ending the condition. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: The Vein Was Promised
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, one creature the duchess can see within 60 feet that has taken no damage since the start of her last turn. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to break the ore binding, ending the condition.

reaction.name: Spurn the Poorer Vein
entries: Trigger: A creature that has taken damage since the start of the duchess's last turn hits her with an attack roll. Response: The duchess gains a +3 bonus to AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

trait.name: Anchored
entries: A standing ledger of red leather, open on a brass post, its ribbons running out to everyone who owes, stands in the debt's space and is part of its body. It has AC 14, 35 Hit Points, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and it can't move on its own. A creature can attack it, or take an action within 5 feet of it to cover it with an opaque cloth. While it is destroyed or covered, Collects What Is Owed does nothing, and the debt can take an action to uncover it. Destroying it deals no damage to the debt.

trait.name: Collects What Is Owed
entries: Once on its turn, immediately after hitting a creature that has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition caused by the debt, the debt can move up to 20 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks or teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 10 feet of that creature. A creature within 5 feet of a charmed target can take an action to tear that target's ledger ribbon, ending the condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The debt makes two Ledger Lash attacks.

action.name: Ledger Lash
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 60 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Collect the Ribbon {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}, one creature the debt can see within 60 feet that has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition caused by it. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only. Either way, the Charmed condition then ends on that creature.

bonus.name: The Account Is Still Open
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}, one creature the debt can see within 60 feet that can hear its invitation and isn't behind Total Cover. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition caused by the debt until the end of its next turn, and a visible ribbon runs from the ledger to it. The condition doesn't compel the target to attack its allies or hand over anything.

reaction.name: Transfer the Account
entries: Trigger: A creature within 30 feet ends the debt's {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition on another creature. Response: The debt teleports up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This doesn't reapply the condition.

trait.name: Crowded Ground
entries: The inquisitor is made of neighbors and is strongest where they stand close. It has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that has another creature within 5 feet of it, and Disadvantage on attack rolls against a creature that has no other creature within 15 feet of it.

trait.name: Judges the Fallen Short
entries: The inquisitor has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that has failed a saving throw against it since the start of the inquisitor's previous turn. A creature that is willingly {@condition Prone|XPHB} is never a target for this, and the inquisitor can't renew the judgment on it.
A creature that is willingly Prone is never a target for this, and the inquisitor can't renew the judgment on it.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The inquisitor makes two Sentence attacks.

action.name: Sentence
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 60 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Sentence of Stillness {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}, one creature the inquisitor can see within 60 feet that can hear it. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Radiant damage, and the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of the inquisitor's next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only. The inquisitor can't use this action against a creature that is willingly Prone.

bonus.name: Kneel and Be Counted
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}, one creature the inquisitor can see within 60 feet that can hear its command and is not willingly {@condition Prone|XPHB}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the Prone condition. A creature can submit instead by dropping Prone willingly at the start of its turn, which requires no action; standing up again costs movement as usual.

reaction.name: Objection
entries: Trigger: A creature the inquisitor can see within 30 feet succeeds on a saving throw against it. Response: The inquisitor moves up to 15 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This doesn't change the result of the save.

monster.name: Pathless Mother

trait.name: Underleaf
entries: While the mother is within 5 feet of a tree, undergrowth, or its own roots, it has Half Cover (a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws) and moves through those spaces without spending extra movement. Burning or clearing the growth around it, or drawing it into open ground, takes this away.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries: If the mother fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Takes the Ones Who Stray
entries: Once on each of its turns, when the mother hits a creature that has no conscious ally within 30 feet of it, it deals an extra 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Slashing damage. A creature that keeps a conscious ally within 30 feet is never a target for this.

trait.name: Rooted to Company
entries: The mother has Disadvantage on Opportunity Attack rolls against a creature that has a conscious ally within 5 feet of it.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The mother makes two Lost Road attacks.

action.name: Lost Road
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 15 ft. {@h}24 ({@damage 4d8 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Turn the Trail {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 18}, up to two creatures the mother can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

Two pale trail stones rise in unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of the mother and remain until the start of her next turn. A creature within 5 feet of a stone can take an action to end the Blinded condition the mother caused on itself or on a creature within 5 feet of it.

bonus.name: The Road Bends to Her
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 18}, one Large or smaller creature the mother can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The mother pulls the target up to 35 feet directly toward herself along an unobstructed path, ending in an unoccupied space, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 18}) from a visible root tether until the start of her next turn. She can maintain only one tether, and a creature within 5 feet of the target can take an action to cut it.

legendaryHeader: Legendary Action Uses: 3. Immediately after another creature's turn, the mother can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary.name: Into the Undergrowth
entries: It moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If it ends this movement within 5 feet of a tree or undergrowth, it can take the Hide action.

legendary.name: Lost Road (Costs 2 Uses)
entries: The mother makes one Lost Road attack.

legendary.name: Move the Milestone
entries: The mother chooses a 10-foot square on a surface she can see within 60 feet. Until the start of her next turn, that square is visibly Difficult Terrain for creatures other than her. She can maintain only one such square.

monster.name: Undertoll

trait.name: Tidebound

entries.name: Description
entries: A forearm and hand, severed cleanly above the elbow, grey and swollen to twice its proper size and bound in knotted kelp. There is no wound where it ends, only a cuff of salt-white shell. It lies under ankle-deep surf, fingers spread, and does not move until something warm steps over it.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A tidewrack hand owns about forty feet of one beach. It does not hunt; it waits at the place where people cross from dry stone into the water, which on most shores is the same four or five flat rocks everyone has used for a century. It wants the crossing kept frightening, and it is content to take one ankle a season.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Children stop using a particular stepping stone and cannot explain why. Crab pots set at that spot come up with the lines wound tight anticlockwise.

entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: The shallows at the old slipway pull harder than they should, even at slack water.
A crewman of the Marion drowned in two feet of water with his boots still laced.
There is a whole drowned man under the sand there, and only his hand has worked loose.
Salt thrown on the water keeps it down.

entries: The first two are true. There is no drowned man, and salt does nothing.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It is only dangerous in the water. A creature standing on dry rock is almost safe from it, and the hand that follows onto stone is slow, clumsy, and easy to break.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Open with the grip, not the sight: have a character feel fingers close on an ankle before anyone sees what has hold of them. It is a first-session monster, and its job is to teach the table that these things obey rules. Let the party work out within two rounds that the beach is safe and the water is not.

entries.name: Description
entries: A squat, headless animal of root and bark, about the size of a dog. Its ribcage is a cage of bark staves, and inside it, turned sideways, is a single human ear. Clusters of closed seed-eyes run down its spine and never open. It moves on thin root toes and it is always, visibly, listening.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A rootlisten owns a household: one cottage, one clearing, one family's private conversations. It does not want the family dead. It wants them careful, and a household that has learned to whisper indoors and say nothing on the path is a household it can live beside for years.

Clan: Deep forest. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Trail marks loop back on themselves; a Hush decree forbids singing the lost-road ballad.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Say anything aloud under those trees and something moves toward you.
It repeats what you said back in your own voice before it comes.
It cannot hear you if you stay still.
Burning the undergrowth drives it out.

entries: The first, second and fourth are true. Standing still does not help; silence does.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It works entirely on speech. It cannot frighten anyone who has not spoken aloud or cast with a verbal component since its last turn, and its reaction only triggers on sound. Fire also strips the cover it fights from.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Use it to establish the forest clan's rule at the lowest possible stakes. It is a nuisance, not a threat, and the correct outcome is that the party learns to shut up in this forest before they meet something that matters. If a caster insists on verbal components, let it work — then let them see what it costs them.

entries.name: Description
entries: A knee-high tangle of soaked netting folded around a circular, lipless mouth of small hooked teeth. Fishing hooks serve it as jointed feet. Two black pearls sit where eyes would be, and the mesh is still caught with the silver scales of an ordinary catch. Hauled aboard, it lies exactly as dead gear lies.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A netmouth owns a boat rather than a stretch of water, and travels with it. It lives in the pile of gear at the stern, eats what it can take from a crew of four or five, and is careful never to take so many that the boat stops going out. A harbor that has one usually has several, each on its own hull.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Empty nets turn toward shore before it appears, and the Hush has quietly removed names from the harbor rolls.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Gear left on deck overnight is found moved, always closer to where the crew sleep.
It can only be killed by burning the whole net, which means burning the boat.
It plays dead until something warm touches it; a boat hook is safe, a bare hand is not.
It came up in a haul off the Ninestones in the famine year.

entries: The first and third are true. Fire hurts it badly but does not require the boat; the Ninestones story is told about every netmouth on the coast.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Fire is its real weakness: any burn strips the armor it takes from a frightened crew for a round. It also cannot frighten anyone who has not touched the net, so a crew that works the gear with gaffs and hooks is far safer than one that works it by hand.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Describe the heap of net twice before it moves, once when the party boards and once when they search. The monster is a punishment for a careless action, so make the careless action available and let someone take it. On a small deck its ability to share a space makes it genuinely frightening at low level.

entries.name: Description
entries: A squat figure the size of a child, cast in candle tallow over a frame of pit props, with a lamp-flame burning somewhere inside its chest where the wax has gone translucent. Its knuckles are iron. It knocks on the rock the way a trapped man knocks, in threes, and then it waits the way a trapped man waits.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A tallow knocker owns one district of one mine: a few hundred yards of roadway and the men who work it. It wants the knocking believed in. A crew that has learned to stop and listen every time is a crew working slowly and fearfully, which is exactly the condition it lives on, and it will go years without killing anyone.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Ventilation doors are found sealed that nobody sealed; the lodge's accident book has pages gummed together.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Three knocks means the door has gone and you have about a minute.
It will not come near a man with an open lamp.
It is the last of the Hallow Drift crew, still knocking.
Safety lamps are no protection; the flame has to be bare.

entries: The second and fourth are true. The knocking means nothing in particular, and no crew it belongs to ever existed.

entries.name: The counter
entries: An uncovered open flame within thirty feet takes away its attack accuracy and its bonus action outright. A covered safety lamp does nothing — which is a cruel joke, since safety lamps are what miners actually carry.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The lamp rule is the lesson of the whole mines clan, so teach it here at CR 1. Put the party underground with safety lamps and let them work out that they need to open one, and that opening one in a gassy roadway is its own decision. It fights from the dark and retreats into it.

entries.name: Description
entries: A broad, swollen figure in the shape of an adult relative, blue-grey and crusted with salt, its throat lengthened by a hand's width so the voice carries. Weed and abandoned netting hang from its shoulders like a coat. It carries nothing and threatens nothing. It stands at the tide line and says names.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A drowned caller owns a parish of perhaps two hundred people and intends to keep every one of them. It works at dusk at the edge of the water, calling the names of the living in the voices of their dead, and it only ever takes those who answer. A household that has learned not to answer can live inside its territory for three generations, which is exactly what the caller wants.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Someone's drowned relative is heard calling from the water at dusk; the parish register has pages cut out where the drowned should be.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It calls in the voice of someone you have lost, and it gets the voice exactly right.
If you answer it even once, it can always find you afterward.
It cannot come above the tide line.
Speaking its own name back to it destroys it.

entries: The first two are true. It can leave the water, though it is much weaker on dry ground, and nothing is destroyed by naming.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It cannot frighten anyone who has stayed silent. A party that works the shore without speaking aloud — no shouted orders, no verbal spellcasting — strips it of its central ability entirely, and that constraint is worth the whole encounter.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is the monster that teaches a table to read a rule. Run it twice if you can: once as an event the party only witnesses, from a window, where a neighbor answers and is taken; and once as a fight, after they have worked out what answering costs. The silence constraint makes casters re-plan, which is the point.

entries.name: Description
entries: A tall figure built out of driftwood and salt crust, hollow through the chest where a body should be, arms permanently open in the shape of an embrace that has nothing in it. It always faces the water. Wood grain runs the wrong way across its face, which has no features except the direction it is turned.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A shorewaiter owns the waiting itself. Its territory is any shore where people still come to watch for ships, and the people it wants are the ones who keep coming. It is not hostile to strangers and does not hunt the parish. It becomes dangerous only when someone tries to take a waiting person away from the water, or when a rival monster comes for the same widows.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of longing. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Driftwood stacks itself into standing figures along the high-water mark; the Hush has twice relocated the village and twice it has walked back.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It has never hurt anyone from this village.
It fought something in the water two winters ago and the sea boiled for an hour.
If you take a widow off that beach it will follow you inland.
It is the ship's figurehead, come back without the ship.

entries: The first three are true. It has no connection to any figurehead, though every coastal village tells that version.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It does not attack a party that leaves its waiting people alone, and it will fight other coast monsters for them. Beyond that, it preys on whoever is isolated: nobody who keeps an ally within thirty feet is a target for its reaching.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Offer it as an alliance before offering it as a fight. The cleanest use is a three-way encounter on a beach: the party, a drowned caller that wants the same widows, and the shorewaiter, which will spend itself on the caller if the party stands aside. If the party does attack it, punish spreading out — it pulls one character away and works on them alone.

entries.name: Description
entries: A high funeral chair of black oak, worn pale on the arms, that walks. A place is laid at it — cloth, cup, plate — and the place is never filled. What sits in the chair is only visible as an absence with weight, and the chair carries it from house to house.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A last seat owns a parish's funeral tables. It attends. It takes the empty place at every wake in its district and it stays until the household has stopped setting one, at which point it comes for them. Its subjects keep mourning on schedule because they have learned what happens when they stop.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of grief. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: A place is laid every night for someone long dead and the household cannot say who started it; licensed mourning hours end early by decree.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It sits down at wakes. If you are hosting, you lay the extra place.
It gets stronger while there are wounded near the dead.
Throw a cloth over the chair and it is blind and harmless.
It is the first person this parish buried.

entries: The first three are true. It was never a person.

entries.name: The counter
entries: The chair is the organ, and it can be covered. A creature within five feet can spend an action to throw an opaque cloth over it — or simply destroy it, AC 12 and 15 Hit Points — and the seat stops healing from the wounded entirely. It can spend its own action to uncover it again.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is the clan's teaching encounter: the furniture is the monster, and the party should work that out by hitting the chair by accident. A funeral in progress makes the best arena, because the wounded and the dead are already in the room. Its vigil attack needs a line of sight to the chair, so covering it does double duty.

entries.name: Description
entries: Nothing is ever seen of it but a shape, and the shape is enormous. In three generations of accounts it is a hunched herder's silhouette standing in its own cold fog, taller than the harbor cranes, moving boats the way a shepherd moves sheep. The bell that sounds with it does not exist; no bell on this coast makes that note.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A haar shepherd owns a harbor and the three miles of water outside it. It does not sink boats. It herds them: away from the channel, onto the bar, into each other, and back to the quay empty, which is the state in which this harbor has received its boats for sixty years. The town has not moved and will not, and that is the shepherd's whole achievement.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Fog rolls in against the wind and against the tide; the Hush licenses funerals here in batches, once a season, to keep the mourning short.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Boats come back crewless, tied off properly, with the catch still aboard.
You can hear a bell in the haar that is not the harbor bell.
It cannot cross into lamplight.
It is the drowned of the Cormorant, all of them together.

entries: The first three are true. It is not made of the dead; it is made of sixty years of the living being afraid of the fog.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Bright light breaks it. It cannot frighten anyone standing in a lit area, and a struck bell clears its fog for thirty feet around the sound. A boat crew with lanterns and a bell can cross its water; one without is working inside its territory on its terms.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Give the party the counter as salvage, not as a lore check: a lantern locker and a hand bell aboard the wreck they are searching. The fight should be run as a chase across open water with visibility as the real resource. Thunder damage grounds it briefly, which rewards a party that works out that it is held up by the weather.

entries.name: Description
entries: A giant built from a counting house: a torso of ledgers and tally sticks, iron measuring rods for arms, and a face that is a single ruled page of fractions. Where a miner lost a hand, a foot, an eye, there is a corresponding figure written on it, and the figures are all less than one.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A redmeasure owns a mining valley and the arithmetic done in it. It does not want the owners dead — it wants the ledger kept, which means it wants the injuries to continue being entered as fractions and the men to keep being angry about it. It breaks doors at night and it takes a count in the morning.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of rage. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Pay is short by the same amount in every purse; the Hush has broken up two meetings in the valley this year.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It comes for whoever hit it last, and it remembers how many.
If you all go at it at once it hits back harder.
It cannot be hurt by anything the company owns.
It is fire-proof.

entries: The first, second and fourth are true. It can be hurt by anything at all.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It tallies attackers, not attacks. The extra damage it returns scales with how many different creatures hit it since its last turn, so a party that lets one character do the striking keeps the tally at one die; a party that all piles in takes the full count back.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Say the tally out loud each round — 'that is three of you now' — so the mechanic is visible by the second turn. It rewards a party that nominates a tank and punishes the instinct to focus-fire with everyone. Its reaction closes the distance to whoever hurt it, so a back-rank character who takes a shot will have it in their face.

entries.name: Description
entries: An ooze that has taken the shape of a tenement wall and is slowly coming off it. Lead-framed windows float in the mass, and the one at its center is lit, warm, and furnished, showing a room nobody in this quarter has. The rest of it is grey and climbing.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A window envier owns one square and the four streets off it. It keeps the lit room visible from every window in the district, and it keeps the district looking. Its people are poorer each year and more certain that the money went somewhere specific, which is the condition it lives in.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of envy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: A house across the square is warm and lit all winter and nobody can say who lives there; rents rise in handwriting no clerk admits to.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: There is a room in it that is better than any room you have been in.
It wants whoever is unhurt. Once you are bleeding it loses interest.
The window can be put out.
Whatever you see in the window is a real room somewhere in the city.

entries: The first three are true. The room is not anywhere.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Its armor depends on there being someone unhurt in sight. Once every creature it can see has taken damage, there is nothing left for it to envy and the Resistance ends.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The charm it offers is harmless on purpose — it does not compel anyone to attack a friend or hand anything over; it just makes them unwilling to walk away from the window. Play that as the horror. The party's own untouched character is the thing keeping its armor on, which is an unpleasant and interesting fact for them to discover.

entries.name: Description
entries: A long-limbed beast, deer-boned and grinning, that has been dancing for so long its feet are gone to the ankle and it goes on anyway. A split fiddle is strapped against its exposed ribs, playing itself. It is genuinely, horribly delighted to see anyone.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A merry unending owns a tavern district's best night and refuses to let it end. Its people are not miserable — that is the difficulty. They are exhausted, euphoric, and unable to go home, and the district has been at its own party for eleven years. It takes the ones who fall down.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of joy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: The same night is celebrated continuously and nobody can name the occasion; three publicans have been relocated by the Hush without explanation.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It takes whoever goes down. Get up and it goes looking elsewhere.
Cover your ears and you cannot hear the fiddle, and it cannot put you down.
The fiddle can be broken.
If you dance with it willingly it will let you go at dawn.

entries: The first three are true. Nobody has ever been let go.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Two doors out. Getting up ends its extra damage immediately — standing is a normal action and it imposes no penalty on doing so — and covering both ears with an action stops a creature hearing the fiddle until it frees a hand. The fiddle itself is AC 13, 25 Hit Points.

entries.name: Running it
entries: It knocks the party down and then dances on them, so the fight has a rhythm: fall, stand, fall. Its reaction lunges at whoever stands up, which makes standing a decision rather than a reflex. A character who gives up both hands to cover their ears is safe and disarmed, which is the same trade the whole district has made.

entries.name: Description
entries: A tree-sized body of split timber and hanging root, with mourning bells grown through the trunk at every height. The bells are the wrong shape, cast in grief rather than bronze, and they are all silent. Where the bark is open the wood underneath is wet and red. It smells of pollen and turned earth.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A bellwound owns a wooded province and the burials in it. It wants the dead to stay out of reach of the parish bells, which means out of the churchyards and under the leaves, and it wants the living to keep going out to look for them. It is patient on a scale of decades, and it does not need to kill anyone to be fed.

Clan: Deep forest. Born of grief. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Burials out in the trees are found disturbed and recovered; a mourning period was cut short by decree and the village obeyed without argument.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It rings when someone dies within a mile, and only the dying hear it.
It heals while there is someone bleeding near a body.
It is afraid of fire.
The bells are from the drowned chapel and can be rung to banish it.

entries: The first three are true. The bells are part of it and cannot be rung by anyone.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It heals only while it can see a badly wounded creature or someone standing near a corpse — getting people above half their Hit Points shuts that down. It is also vulnerable to fire, and it fights from cover that burns.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Make its healing legible: say the wood closes when it heals, and say what it is looking at. The party should work out that keeping each other topped up is more valuable than extra damage. Its deafening and blinding stack onto its own saves, so a party that ignores the conditions will fail more of them — but any ally can spend an action to clear one.

entries.name: Description
entries: An elemental of ore and seam-water in the shape of a woman wearing a mine: galleries for skirts, a coronet of unworked silver, and a body that is cross-sectioned so the good vein is visible running through her. She is scrupulously polite and takes only from those who have not yet been hurt.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A seam duchess owns a mining village through its envy. She reserves the richest seam, visibly, for nobody, and lets the village watch it. Her subjects do not leave, because the vein is still there and might yet be theirs, and she takes a little from the ones who are still whole and lucky.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of envy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: A seam is found opened and worked by no crew; the owners' favor lists are posted and then withdrawn by decree.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: She takes whoever is still untouched. Get a scratch and she loses interest.
The vein she guards is real and it is the richest in the county.
She cannot be struck by a man who has taken her wages.
She will bargain, and she keeps her word.

entries: The first, second and fourth are true. Wages have nothing to do with it.

entries.name: The counter
entries: She envies the unhurt. A creature that has taken no damage since the start of her last turn is the one she wants, and once everyone has been hurt she has nothing left to want from them.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The counter is counter-intuitive and should be discovered as such: the safest character at her table is the one who is already bleeding. Her reaction protects her specifically from the wounded, which means the party's damaged frontliner has a harder time landing hits than its untouched wizard — and the wizard is the one she is coming for.

entries.name: Description
entries: A tall, courteous fiend in worn red velvet, with a standing ledger on a brass post growing out of its hip. Ribbons run from the ledger to everyone who owes it, and the ribbons are visible to everyone in the room. It is unfailingly polite and it does not hurry.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A velvet debt owns a brothel district through its accounts. It did not come from the people who worked there; it came from the clients who believed that paying bought permanence. It keeps a quarter in debt, and it is careful to keep its debtors working, housed, and unable to leave.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of lust. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Debts in the district are recorded as settled and remain owed; a house is relocated and its ledger is not.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Everyone it has a hold on has a ribbon. You can see them.
Cut somebody's ribbon and the hold ends.
It never makes anyone hurt their friends.
Pay the debt off and it has no claim.

entries: The first three are true. The debt cannot be paid; that is the whole of it.

entries.name: The counter
entries: The ribbons are the counter and they are deliberately, visibly cuttable: any creature within five feet of a charmed ally can spend an action to tear that ribbon and end the condition. The ledger itself is AC 14, 35 Hit Points, and covering or destroying it stops the fiend's pursuit entirely.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Its charm is non-compelling by design — it never turns a character against the party — so the horror is in the ribbon, not in losing control. Keep saying who is tied to it. Its reaction teleports it away whenever somebody cuts a ribbon, which turns the fight into a pursuit through rooms it keeps leaving.

entries.name: Description
entries: A man-shaped thing in clean civic dress, carrying no weapon and no warrant. Its face is a parish seal. It speaks in sentences that have already been handed down, and where it walks the pavement is swept. It is made entirely of a city's certainty that it is better than its neighbors.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A parish inquisitor owns a city's good opinion of itself. It patrols the boundary with the next settlement, it judges travelers at the gate, and it makes examples. Its subjects are proud, obedient, and unwilling to be the one it stops, and it has never needed to kill more than a few of them a year.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of pride. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Visitors are judged at a gate by a court that never convenes; a neighbouring village's name has been struck from the civic rolls.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It cannot touch you if you kneel.
It only presses the ones who have already failed in front of it.
It judges by the law of this city, which is not written down.
It can be appealed to, in the correct form.

entries: The first three are true. There is no appeal, and the correct form does not exist.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Kneeling works, literally. A creature that is willingly Prone is never a target for its judgment, cannot be hit by its Sentence of Stillness, and cannot have the judgment renewed on it. Dropping prone costs nothing at the start of a turn; standing back up costs movement.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The decision the fight asks for is whether to kneel to it, and that should feel bad. A kneeling character is safe and useless. Let the party find the rule early and then spend the rest of the encounter choosing, round by round, who is standing up. Its reaction moves it whenever someone resists successfully, so it circles the ones who will not bow.

entries.name: Description
entries: Huge and many-limbed, built out of the roads that used to run here: packed earth, milestones, broken paving, and the boots of travelers, all grown into a maternal shape with too many arms and no face. Trail stones rise around her when she moves. She is always turned toward whoever is furthest from the group.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A pathless mother owns a province's roads. She does not close them; she unties them, so that every route still exists and none of them arrives. Her people stay — they are waiting for the road home to work again — and she takes only the ones who go on ahead, fall behind, or set out alone.

Clan: Deep forest. Born of longing. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Trail marks loop back on themselves; the Hush has forbidden the lost-road ballad in three counties and hanged two people for singing it.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Nobody who walks out of this province alone walks out of it at all.
The milestones move when you are not looking at them.
She will not touch you while someone has hold of you.
She is looking for her own children and will stop if you help her find them.

entries: The first three are true. She is not looking for anyone; she is the shape of a province that is.

entries.name: The counter
entries: She can only take the extra from a creature with no conscious ally within thirty feet, and her opportunity attacks are weak against anyone standing with a friend. Her own trail stones are the counter to her blindness: a character beside one can spend an action to clear it from themselves or a neighbor.

entries.name: Running it
entries: She pulls one character out of the line every round — that is the whole fight. Run her as an attempt to break the party into individuals, and let the party's answer be discipline. Her trail stones appear as a side effect of her own recharge action, so the counter arrives on her schedule; point them out the first time, then stop.

entries.name: Description
entries: A mass the size of a chapel, grey and water-logged, built out of the shapes of carried coffins and the arms that carried them. Bells are set into it at every level, all of them full of silt and none of them able to ring. It moves the way a tide moves, without hurry and without being resisted, and it keeps the drowned inside it where the parish can see them.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: An undertoll owns an entire coastline and every funeral on it. It does not need to kill in order to feed; it needs the dead to stay unrecovered and the living to stay wounded about it. Where it rules, the tide gives nothing back, and whole coast parishes organize their year around a grief they are never permitted to finish.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of grief. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: The sea stops returning bodies for a hundred miles; mourning periods are cut short by decree and nobody objects aloud.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Nothing this coast loses is ever given back, not wreckage, not cargo, not people.
It grows stronger while there are wounded near the dead.
It will not touch anyone who has never lost someone to the water.
The bells inside it are from the drowned chapel at Verrick.

entries: The first two are true. It has no interest in whether you have lost anyone, and the bells are its own.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It heals only while it can see someone badly hurt near a corpse. Dragging the wounded clear of the dead, breaking its line of sight, or simply healing people above half shuts the regeneration off — and it actively prevents the first of those by holding corpses in place.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Make the corpses a battlefield feature, not scenery: the party arrives at a shore already strewn with the morning's drowned, and where they fight decides whether it heals. Its reaction drags it toward anyone who drops, so going down near the bodies is a trap. A party that fights it on dry stone, away from the dead, can kill it; one that fights it in the surf among corpses will not.

entries.name: Description
entries: A construct the size of a gatehouse, built from sealed record chests, lead strapping, and wax. It has no face, only a slot. It is extraordinarily heavy and makes almost no sound moving, and where it stands, conversation nearby gets quieter without anyone deciding to be quiet.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A hushweight owns a capital's archive and, through it, the capital. It does not suppress the records for anyone's benefit; it is made of the fear that they will be read, and it farms that fear by existing visibly and never being opened. Its subjects are an entire city that has agreed not to ask.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: A public square is cleared of people on no stated authority; three archivists are reassigned in one week and none are seen again.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Say out loud what you have seen it do and its armor opens for a moment.
It cannot be hurt while anyone nearby is afraid of it.
Whatever is inside it is worse than it is.
It is deaf, so speaking is safe.

entries: The first two are true. Nothing is inside it, and it is not deaf.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Testimony is the counter, and it costs an action: a creature within thirty feet can take an action to say aloud one true thing it has watched the hushweight do, and its Resistance drops until the start of its next turn. Being Deafened does not stop a character speaking; being magically silenced does. Blinding it shuts the Resistance off entirely.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is an action-economy fight dressed as a moral one. Somebody has to spend their turn testifying instead of attacking, every round, and the party has to decide who can afford to. Make the testimony diegetic — ask the player what their character says — and the encounter will do more work than its stat block suggests.

entries.name: Description
entries: Huge, and torn open from the inside. A giant made of shaft timbers, winding cable, and the coats of a whole shift, split down the chest so the firedamp burning inside is visible. It carries nothing. It does not need to: everything it has to say it says by bringing a roof down.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A pit reprisal owns a province's anger at its employers. It does not destroy the mines — that would end the grievance. It takes shift managers, it collapses the workings of companies that have been warned, and it leaves the men alive and furious, which is the crop it farms.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of rage. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Known-bad workings are sent crews anyway and the crews are not seen again; the Hush burns the inquest records before they are read.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It only ever comes for the ones who sent the shift down.
It gets worse the more of you hit it.
Cold water will make it let go of anything.
It can be reasoned with if you show it the ledger.

entries: The first three are true. It cannot be reasoned with at all; nothing can.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Like every rage-born thing it tallies attackers. Striking it with one character instead of four keeps the return damage to a single die. Cold damage makes it rupture free of a grapple and empties its tally for a round, which is a real tactical trade for a party that has it held.

entries.name: Running it
entries: A collapsing mine is the arena, and its line attack should bring part of it down. The cold-damage reaction is a lever the party can pull deliberately: it escapes the grapple, but its tally resets, so a party that has been piling on can use a frost spell to wipe the count. Let them find that.

entries.name: Description
entries: Huge, and still in evening dress a generation out of date. A brass bandstand has grown through its shoulders and is still playing the tune from the victory night. Below the knee it is bone and splinter. It dances on a floor it brings with it, and the floor does not let people up.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A last dance owns a generation's refusal to admit that the war came back. Its territory is a capital's pleasure district, and its subjects are everyone who was at that party and everyone who has heard about it. It keeps the night running and it takes those who fall out of the dancing.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of joy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: No musician for miles can finish a tune, stopping two bars short without knowing why; dancing is licensed here and most permits are refused.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It takes whoever is on the floor. Get them up.
Someone else can haul you up without costing you anything.
Deafen it and it slows right down.
It will stop at dawn, as it did that night.

entries: The first three are true. It has not stopped in forty years.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Getting people up is the whole defense, and the stat block makes it cheap: a creature within five feet can spend an action to haul a prone ally upright without spending that ally's movement. Deafening it halves its Speed and shuts off both its extra attack and its area action.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Run it as an action-economy problem. Every round it puts people down and somebody has to spend a turn picking them up, which is exactly how the district has spent forty years. Deafness is the win condition and should be reachable — thunder, silence, a good shove into the harbor — and when the party finds it, let the fight visibly collapse.

entries.name: Description
entries: A huge walking room. Clay walls sag like skin, shroud curtains hang as four thick legs, and a tarnished doorway stands in its front face, open on a parlor with the chairs set and nobody in them. Mirrors inside it are intact and show the room as it should be.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A returned room owns a nation's war dead, or rather the houses they did not come back to. Its territory is every cemetery district in the country, and it spends its time visiting the homes of the missing and standing in the street outside. Its people keep the rooms ready, which is what it is for.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of grief. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Houses are found with one more room than they were built with, furnished and cold; graves reopen from the inside, empty and tidy.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: There is a door in it and the room behind the door is your room.
Radiant light opens its armor.
Healing somebody next to it opens its armor too.
Anyone it swallows is in the parlor and can be fetched out.

entries: The first three are true. There is no parlor; what it takes, it digests.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Its Resistance drops for a round whenever it takes Radiant damage, or whenever a creature within five feet of it heals someone else. The doorway it grapples with can be hauled open by any creature within five feet, which frees the victim.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The healing counter is the good one: a cleric standing next to the monster, patching someone up, is strictly better than a cleric standing back. Its grapple takes one character out of the fight into a room where the chairs are set, which is the image the whole encounter is for. Describe the parlor before you describe the acid.

entries.name: Description
entries: A dragon only in build: gargantuan, antlered, with a crest of bark plates that opens on a single enormous eye. Its body is forest floor — leaf litter, standing water, fallen trunks — assembled into something that walks. Behind it the forest is visibly a different forest, and the party has not moved.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A country behind trees owns everything a generation is afraid of in the woods. It does not have a den. Its territory is the wrongness itself, which spreads along trails, and its subjects are everyone within a day's walk who has stopped using the forest after dark. It is perfectly happy for them to go on living at the edge of it.

Clan: Deep forest. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Roads walked twice arrive in two different places; every map of this forest is accurate on the day it is drawn and wrong by the next.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: There is a country behind the trees and the path into it is any path at all.
Do not look at the eye on its crest.
It cannot find you if you keep your eyes off it.
Iron nailed to a trunk marks a true path.

entries: The first three are true. Iron does nothing, though half the province has nailed it up anyway.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Everything it does with fear runs through the open eye on its crest. A creature that averts its gaze at the start of its turn cannot see the dragon, and the dragon can neither frighten it nor deal its extra damage to it for that round. Radiant damage shuts the crest for a round as well.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The averted-gaze rule should be discovered, then should cost something: blind characters cannot pick targets well, so the party has to decide each round who is looking. Its lair actions turn paths and close the trees, so the arena is in motion. Run it as a fight the party cannot leave rather than one they cannot win.

entries.name: Description
entries: Gargantuan and almost entirely buried, so that what the party fights is a face and two hands coming up out of worked stone. It is made of the wealth taken out of the ground, compressed: ore, coin, cut gems, and the dark between them. Its mouth is a shaft. Its thoughts arrive as weight.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A nation below owns a country's conviction that it is being buried by its own extraction. Its territory is every working in the province and the cities above them. It does not surface. It rules by pressure, and its subjects are a whole nation of people who will not go downstairs.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of fear. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Nobody can say how deep the workings go, and every honest answer is a different number; pit ponies will not pass the second level.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It is under all of us, not just under the mine.
Beating a rhythm on the stone brings your hearing back.
It needs you deaf and afraid both; one or the other is not enough.
The gems in it can be cut out and sold.

entries: The first three are true. Nothing has ever been cut out of it.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Its accuracy bonus needs both conditions at once — Frightened and Deafened. Ending either is enough, and any creature can spend an action to beat an audible rhythm on stone and clear the deafness from itself or a neighbor. A creature that does so also gets the next save against it with Advantage.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Run the deafness as the party's main problem and the rhythm as their main answer; someone has to spend actions drumming on the floor while everyone else fights, which is a good job for a character who has run out of better ones. Its lair actions put out open flames, so the clan's light counter is something the party has to keep re-establishing.

entries.name: Description
entries: A fleet's worth of absence given one body: a gargantuan shape of rigging, empty uniform, and grey water standing upright above the harbor, hung with the ropes of ships that never docked. Where a face should be there is a bare horizon. It does not sail. It presides.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: An admiralty of absence owns a seaboard and the identity of everyone on it. Its people no longer describe themselves as fishermen or traders but as those who wait, and that is the condition it farms. It rules by isolation: it takes people one at a time, off the end of a quay, out of the back of a crowd, and the taking is what keeps the rest waiting.
