Clan: Coast and sea. Born of longing. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: The names of the lost appear scratched into doorposts overnight in the householders' own handwriting; no ship that leaves is sighted again from land.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Everyone here is waiting for someone, and nobody can describe their face any more.
It takes whoever is standing on their own.
A full muster on the quay — everyone, all at once — will drive it off.
It was an admiral once, and it can still be addressed by rank.

entries: The first three are true. It was never a person; the rank is a shape it took from the people who made it.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It is starved by company. It can only take the extra from a creature with no conscious ally within thirty feet, and if three pairs of defenders hold station together its own armor drops. Its rope lines can be cut: AC 15, 20 Hit Points each.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is the formation-discipline fight of the collection. Reward a party that moves as a unit and punish the one that fans out to flank. Its pulls exist to break the formation up, so the tactical loop is: it isolates, the party re-forms, it isolates again. Cutting the lines should feel like the right use of a turn.

entries.name: Description
entries: Gargantuan, assembled from the facades of a capital: brick legs, stained-silk hands, a many-storeyed face set with lead-framed window eyes. At its center one golden room is lit and occupied, and whoever looks at it sees their own life being lived better in there by someone else.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A lord of other windows owns a nation's envy of its capital. Its territory is not a district but a relationship: every provincial town that believes the money went to the city, and the city that believes it deserved it. It takes the untouched and the fortunate, and it leaves the resentment behind intact.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of envy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Every house looks poorer from outside than it is and its neighbor looks richer; anyone who inherits money is not seen in the quarter again, though their letters keep arriving.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It shows you your own life as it should have gone.
Cover the golden room and it stops.
It wants whoever has not been hurt yet.
The room is a window into the palace.

entries: The first three are true. The room is not a window into anything.

entries.name: The counter
entries: The golden room at its center is the organ. Covering or shattering it stops the envy damage until the start of its next turn, which takes an action within five feet or 25 Bludgeoning damage in a single turn. Its own shutter reaction also turns the damage off for a round when it uses it defensively.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The 25-damage threshold is a deliberate invitation to a specialist: a character with a hammer and one good round can switch the monster's main damage off. Its shutter reaction means a party that leans on ranged attacks will keep accidentally disabling its envy, which is a trade worth letting them notice.

entries.name: Description
entries: Gargantuan, respectable, and covered. A grey linen veil is stretched over the place where its face should be and stitched shut at the corners. Beneath the veil the body is immaculate, dressed, and wrong in proportion. It is extremely careful not to be seen, and it brings witnesses everywhere.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: An unconfessed owns a generation's hidden debts and quiet abuses. Its territory is a respectable district, and it keeps the respectability going: it needs the doors closed and the neighbors knowing. Its subjects are people who all know one thing about each other and have agreed never to say it.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of shame. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: No door in the parish stays shut, and nobody is ever found to have opened them; written confessions copy themselves onto the next page in the same hand.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: It needs a witness. It cannot touch you if nobody is near you.
Stand up and it loses its hold.
Blind it and it stops singling people out.
It makes you confess things out loud.

entries: The first three are true. It makes nobody say anything; that is a story the parish tells.

entries.name: The counter
entries: It needs its target prone and within ten feet of another creature. Standing up removes one condition, stepping away from everyone removes the other, and either is enough. Blinding it shuts its extra attack off entirely. The veil is AC 16, 70 Hit Points.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The stat block states explicitly that no player is required to disclose anything, and that line should be read aloud at the table if the subject matter needs it. Mechanically it is the inverse of the city clan: it wants people close together and prone, so the party's answer is to spread out and stay up, which leaves them badly placed for everything else in the district.

entries.name: Description
entries: A gargantuan construct in the shape of a crown and the hands that hold it up, cast in gold over a frame of charters. There is no head beneath it. It has been waiting a long time for somebody to be under it, and it has decided that everybody is.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A crown without subjects owns an empire that no longer exists, and administers it anyway. Its territory is every country that was ever claimed, and its subjects are everyone who happens to be standing in one. It does not need obedience to be sincere; it only needs it to be performed.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of pride. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Oaths sworn in the region bind to the crown whatever words are used; coins come out of the press blank on the ruler's side.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Kneel and it has no hold on you at all.
It is armored by everyone who has just failed in front of it.
It does not hit people who are already down.
There was a king in it once.

entries: The first three are true. There was never anyone in it.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Kneeling strips it. Its Resistance depends on there being someone in sight who recently failed a save against it, and a willingly Prone creature never counts — so a party that all kneels removes its armor outright. It also cannot make opportunity attacks against the kneeling, and its charter blast does them no damage at all.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The whole encounter is a question about dignity with real mechanical weight on both sides, and the right answer is humiliating. A party that kneels wins faster. Let them discover it, let them hate it, and do not soften the fact that it works.

entries.name: Description
entries: Two monsters that have grown into one body and do not match. The lower half is a wreck: hull plate, kelp, drowned bulk, and a great cracked fog bell. Grafted into its back is a parish's mourning wheel, a cartwheel of coffin boards hung with the names of the unrecovered. Each half rings at a different time, and the two sounds do not agree.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A wreck-parish confluence owns a drowned coast and the parish that drowned with it. It wants two things at once — the fear of the deep and the grief of the unreturned — and it keeps the population supplied with both. Its domain is identifiable at a distance by the sound: bells under the water at the wrong hours, and never the full count.

Clan: Coast and sea. Born of fear, grief. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Church bells ring two strokes short all along the coast; the sea returns nothing, and no funeral can be finished at the graveside.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Two things died here and only one thing got up.
Crack the bell and the fog goes out of it.
Break the wheel and it stops healing.
Killing one half kills the whole thing.

entries: The first three are true. Breaking both organs does not kill it; it dies at 0 Hit Points like anything else, and the last stretch is fought against an ordinary, furious wreck.

entries.name: The counter
entries: The two halves have separate counters and fail separately. Dry ground blunts the wreck; keeping the wounded away from the dead starves the parish. Neither counter touches the other, and at 345 and 172 Hit Points the matching organ breaks for good.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Stage this as a three-act fight and say so with description, not with mechanics: the bell cracks audibly at the first threshold, the wheel splits at the second. Players should be able to predict the second break once they have seen the first. Its lair actions raise water and surface corpses, so it actively rebuilds the conditions its own halves need — the party is fighting the terrain as much as the monster.

entries.name: Description
entries: Two forest monsters grown together along an abandoned railway. One face is a watching face, all bark and open eye. The other is hollow, the shape of a doorway with nothing behind it. Between them runs a trunk wrapped in rails, sleepers, and the roots that have pulled them up. Both faces look at you, and only one of them is interested.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A root-and-rail concord owns a forest and the line that was driven through it, and it rules the country on both sides. It wants two things: travelers afraid to be in the trees, and travelers who cannot stop trying to get home. It keeps a province supplied with both, and it keeps the line open, because a railway nobody uses would end the longing it lives on.

Clan: Deep forest. Born of fear, longing. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: A railway runs through the forest that no company laid and none can find to lift; anyone who walks out alone walks out a day late.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Two things came together here and the joint never healed.
Keep your eyes off the watching face and it cannot frighten you.
Stay in pairs and the hollow face has nothing to call.
The last train through still runs, and you can board it.

entries: The first three are true. There is no train; the sound of one is the hollow face calling.

entries.name: The counter
entries: The two faces have separate counters. Averting your gaze stops the watching face; keeping a conscious ally within thirty feet starves the hollow one. Neither counter touches the other, and the faces break for good at 338 and 169 Hit Points.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is the fused fight that asks the party to hold two disciplines at once — eyes down and ranks closed — which is awkward on purpose. Break the watching face first if the party is pressing damage, and let them feel the fight change: after it goes, they can look up, and the whole encounter becomes about formation instead.

entries.name: Description
entries: Two mine-monsters fused and still burning. The lower body is a furnace: brick, slag, and a door standing open on white heat. Set in the shoulders is a counting mask of beaten silver with the owners' features, serene and undamaged. One half is incandescent with rage and the other is calmly taking an inventory.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A furnace of the unpaid owns an industrial age. Its domain is every valley worked by the same company, and it keeps two feelings running in parallel: the fury of the men who were not paid, and their envy of the houses that were. It does not want the company destroyed, because without the company there is nothing to be unpaid by.

Clan: Mountains and mines. Born of rage, envy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Fires in the region cannot be put out with water; the owners' houses stand warm and empty while the valley freezes.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: The furnace half answers whoever hits it. The mask half wants whoever is unmarked.
Crack the furnace and it stops counting your blows.
Break the mask and it stops singling out the lucky ones.
Both of them go out together.

entries: The first three are true. The two organs fail separately, at 390 and 195 Hit Points.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Two independent counters. Striking it with one character keeps the rage tally short; letting everyone take some damage denies the mask its untouched target. Neither counter affects the other, and an open flame still blunts the whole creature through its clan trait.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Its own Stoke action makes its light count as the open flame that weakens it — a monster whose temper undermines its own defense, and worth saying out loud when it happens. Run the two organs as two different opponents sharing a body: the party's tank manages the furnace while everyone else manages the mask.

entries.name: Description
entries: A celestial, and recognizably so: radiant, symmetrical, terrible, and shaped like a walled city standing up. Its mask is a civic face, serene, with every window in the walls behind it serving as an eye. Set into its chest is a throne seal that has judged this country innocent and intends to keep doing so.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A city that watches owns a nation's reputation. It fuses the fear of being seen with the pride of being blameless, and it governs both: everything done out of doors is known by morning, and nothing the city itself did appears in any record. Its subjects are observed, judged, and certain of their own innocence.

Clan: Walled cities. Born of fear, pride. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Anything done out of doors is known correctly by everyone by morning with no source; the city's own crimes are missing from every record kept inside the walls, including records carried in from elsewhere.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Say out loud what you have watched it do and the mask opens for a moment.
Kneel and the seal cannot press you.
The two halves do not fail together.
It is a god, and it can be prayed to.

entries: The first three are true. It is a monster that a nation made; prayer does nothing.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Two counters, independent. Testimony — an action, within thirty feet, one true observed thing — drops the mask's Resistance for a round. Kneeling denies the seal its target. The mask breaks for good at 394 Hit Points and the seal at 197.

entries.name: Running it
entries: Both counters cost the party actions or dignity, and both are worth it. Its lair actions rearrange the streets, so position is never settled. Break the mask first and the fight becomes a straightforward judgment; break the seal first and it becomes a fight against being watched. Let the party's damage decide which story they get.

entries.name: Description
entries: A gargantuan frontage of a building that was three establishments and is now one fiend. A red leather ledger stands on a brass post at one corner; a grey veil hangs at another; a brass bandstand plays at the third. Its doors are all open. Everything inside is still going on.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A house of all last nights owns the whole urban haunt: the brothel's debt, the parish's shame, and the tavern's refusal to close, fused across generations into one landlord. Its territory is a capital's night, and its subjects cannot end an evening, settle an account, or shut a door.

Clan: Urban haunts. Born of lust, shame, joy. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: Nobody within miles can end an evening, arriving home at dawn with no account of the hours; every house has one door its owners did not install and will not open.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: There are three faces on it and they do not want the same thing.
Each one has its own way of being switched off.
The ledger, the veil and the bandstand can all be broken.
Settle your account and it will let you leave.

entries: The first three are true. No account has ever been settled.

entries.name: The counter
entries: Three organs, three counters, all independent. Tear a ledger ribbon to end a charm; stand up to deny both the veil and the bandstand; cover both ears against the music. Each object is AC 17 with 60 Hit Points, and the three faces break for good at 482, 321 and 160 Hit Points.

entries.name: Running it
entries: The capstone of the haunts clan, and it should feel like fighting three monsters that happen to share a frontage. Let the party choose which object to break first and let that choice visibly change what the fight is about. Its teleport never removes anyone from the encounter — it only drags them back toward the house, which is thematically the entire point.

entries.name: Description
entries: Gargantuan beyond the scale of the others, and visibly made of five monsters that have stopped being separate. A fog bell hangs in its flank. A mourning mask is set into its shoulder. A furnace burns in its chest, a jealous window glows at its throat, and a hollow arch stands open in its back. The parts do not agree and it moves anyway.

entries.name: Domain and habits
entries: A country of teeth owns a country. Every other monster in this book takes a household, a parish, a province; this one has eaten five provincial powers and governs what is left as a single estate. There is no settlement inside its borders that is not feeding it, and the Hush has abandoned the region entirely.

Clan: Confluence. Born of fear, grief, rage, envy, longing. It was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough, and it is now independent of them. Nobody's change of heart will unmake it; it has to be destroyed by hand.

entries.name: Signs
entries: No two people inside the borders agree on which country they are standing in, and all of them are correct; the Hush's records end mid-sentence and its officers are among the dead here.

entries.name: What is known
entries: What the people of its domain will tell you, if the Hush has not got to them first:

items: Five things came together and every one of them still has its own rule.
Each organ fails separately, and you can see which one has gone.
Turning off two of its organs at once makes it clumsy.
Kill the right organ and the whole thing dies.

entries: The first three are true. Breaking every organ does not kill it; it dies at 0 Hit Points like anything else.

entries.name: The counter
entries: All five counters from the rest of the book at once: end Frightened, keep the wounded away from the dead, strike it with one character rather than four, let nobody stay untouched, and keep a conscious ally within thirty feet. Holding two at the same time gives Advantage on saves against its line attack. The organs break at 580, 464, 348, 232 and 116 Hit Points.

entries.name: Running it
entries: This is a graduation exam, and it only works if the party has met the other clans. Every rule here is one they have already learned somewhere else, and the fight asks them to hold five disciplines at once while the arena changes underfoot. Call each organ by name when it breaks. By the last hundred Hit Points it should be an ordinary enormous animal, and that should be a relief.

legendaryGroup.name: Admiralty of Absence
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the admiralty takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The water withdraws from the whole shore at once. Each creature standing in water within 120 feet of the admiralty makes a DC 22 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is pulled 20 feet toward the open sea and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

A sail that is not there crosses the sky. Each creature within 120 feet of the admiralty that has no conscious ally within 30 feet of it makes a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw, taking 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.
Grey fog fills the harbor. The lair becomes Lightly Obscured until the end of the admiralty's next turn, and the admiralty can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see within the fog.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the admiralty's shore is altered in the following ways:

items: No vessel that leaves this coast is sighted again from land, whatever its course. Lookouts report an empty horizon even while the vessel is plainly visible from the water.
The names of everyone lost at sea from this parish appear scratched into doorposts and keels overnight, in handwriting the living recognize as their own.
Nobody in the region can describe the face of a person who left by sea. They remember the name, the voyage, and the day, and nothing else.

regionalEffects: If the admiralty dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the names weather off the doorposts last.

legendaryGroup.name: City That Watches
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the city takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: Every window becomes an eye. Each creature within 120 feet of the city makes a DC 25 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the city's next turn.

The square is called to order. Each creature within 90 feet of the city that is not willingly {@condition Prone|XPHB} makes a DC 25 Charisma saving throw, taking 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Radiant damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

The streets rearrange. Each creature within 120 feet of the city is teleported to an unoccupied space the city can see within 30 feet of it. A creature can refuse by succeeding on a DC 25 Wisdom saving throw.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the city's walls is altered in the following ways:

items: Within 6 miles, anything done out of doors is known by morning, correctly, by everyone, with no one able to name a source.
The city's own crimes are absent from every record kept inside its walls, including records written elsewhere and carried in.
Visitors are judged at the gate by a court that does not convene and is never wrong about who they are.

regionalEffects: If the city dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the records fill back in with what was taken out.

legendaryGroup.name: Country Behind Trees
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the country takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: Every path turns. Each creature within 120 feet of the country that is moving along a trail makes a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of the country's next turn.

The trees close ranks. A 30-foot-radius area the country can see within 120 feet fills with thorn and trunk until the end of the country's next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain and grants Half Cover.

The crest opens wide. Each creature within 60 feet of the country that can see its crest makes a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the country's next turn.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the country's forest is altered in the following ways:

items: Trails within 6 miles don't end where they are supposed to. A road walked twice arrives in two different places.
Anyone who sleeps in the forest wakes one mile further in, with their bedding undisturbed and their boots clean.
No map of this forest agrees with another, and all of them are accurate on the day they are drawn.

regionalEffects: If the country dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the trails are the last to settle.

legendaryGroup.name: Country of Teeth
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the country takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The border moves. Each creature within 120 feet of the country makes a DC 26 Strength saving throw or is pulled 20 feet toward it and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

Five mouths speak at once and disagree. Each creature within 90 feet of the country makes a DC 26 Wisdom saving throw, taking 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

The ground remembers another country. A 60-foot-radius area the country can see within 120 feet becomes water, forest floor, worked stone, or city flagstone, the country's choice, until the end of its next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain for creatures other than the country.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the country's borders is altered in the following ways:

items: No two people within 6 miles agree on which country they are standing in, and all of them are correct.
Every feeling in the region is held in common. A private grief becomes a parish's grief inside a day.
The Hush has abandoned this country. Its records end mid-sentence, and its officers are among the dead here.

regionalEffects: If the country dies, these effects end immediately, and the five countries it ate stay eaten.

legendaryGroup.name: Crown Without Subjects
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the crown takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The charter is read. Each creature within 90 feet of the crown that can hear it makes a DC 23 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. A creature that is willingly Prone is unaffected.

The flagstones raise a dais. A 20-foot-radius area the crown can see within 90 feet rises 10 feet until the end of the crown's next turn; creatures in that area when it rises make a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition.

Gold light falls on the unbowed. Each creature within 60 feet of the crown that is not willingly Prone makes a DC 23 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Radiant damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the crown's seat is altered in the following ways:

items: Every oath sworn within 6 miles is sworn to the crown, whatever words are used and whoever is meant.
Coins minted in the region come out blank on the ruler's side, in every press, every time.
Nobody in this country can remember the name of a living monarch, though they are certain they owe one obedience.

regionalEffects: If the crown dies, these effects end immediately, and the next coins struck bear an ordinary face.

legendaryGroup.name: Furnace of the Unpaid
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the furnace takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The shift bell rings. Each creature within 90 feet of the furnace makes a DC 25 Constitution saving throw, taking 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Fire damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

Slag runs across the floor. A 30-foot-radius area the furnace can see within 90 feet is covered in molten slag until the end of the furnace's next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain, and a creature that starts its turn there takes 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Fire damage.

The counting mask reads the roll. Each creature within 60 feet of the furnace that has taken no damage since the start of the furnace's last turn makes a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw or has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of the furnace's next turn.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the furnace's workings is altered in the following ways:

items: No fire within 6 miles can be put out by water. It has to be smothered, or allowed to finish.
Wages paid in this region are short by the same amount in every purse, and the difference is never found.
The owners' houses stand untouched and warm while the valley freezes, and no one has lived in them for years.

regionalEffects: If the furnace dies, these effects end immediately, and the first fire lit afterward goes out in water as it should.

legendaryGroup.name: House of All Last Nights
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the house takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The band strikes up. Each creature within 90 feet of the house that can hear the bandstand makes a DC 26 Dexterity saving throw or has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

Ribbons run out from the ledger. Each creature within 60 feet of the house makes a DC 26 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition caused by the house until the end of the house's next turn. A creature within 5 feet of a charmed creature can take an action to tear the ribbon, ending the condition.

Every private room opens onto the floor. Each creature within 90 feet of the house makes a DC 26 Charisma saving throw, taking 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success. No player is required to disclose anything.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the house is altered in the following ways:

items: Nobody within 6 miles can end an evening. They arrive home at dawn with no account of the hours and no wish to give one.
Debts contracted in this region are never settled. Payment is accepted, recorded, and the debt stands.
Every house in the district has one door its owners did not install and will not open.

regionalEffects: If the house dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the extra doors are bricked up by neighbors who will not discuss them.

legendaryGroup.name: Last Dance
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the dance takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The tune starts again from the top. Each creature within 60 feet of the dance that can hear the bandstand makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
The floorboards buckle into steps. A 30-foot-radius area the dance can see within 90 feet becomes Difficult Terrain until the end of the dance's next turn.

Lamps gutter and the hall fills with the crowd that isn't there. Each creature within 60 feet of the dance makes a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw, taking 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the dance's hall is altered in the following ways:

items: No musician within 6 miles can finish a tune. Players stop two bars from the end and cannot say why.
Everyone in the district dreams the same night, the one before the war, and wakes certain it was last night.
Dancing is a licensed activity here. The Hush issues permits, refuses most of them, and will not explain the refusals.

regionalEffects: If the dance dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the last thing to go is the dreaming.

legendaryGroup.name: Lord of Other Windows
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the lord takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: Every window lights at once. Each creature within 120 feet of the lord that can see a lit window makes a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

The square narrows. A 40-foot-radius area the lord can see within 120 feet is crowded with facades until the end of the lord's next turn; that area is Difficult Terrain, and the lord has Advantage on attack rolls against creatures within it.
The lord trades two rooms. Two creatures the lord can see within 90 feet each make a DC 22 Charisma saving throw, and each creature that fails swaps places with the other.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the lord's quarter is altered in the following ways:

items: Every house within 6 miles looks poorer from the outside than it is, and its neighbor looks richer than it is.
Rents in the quarter rise overnight, in handwriting no clerk admits to, and are always paid.
A person who inherits money in this region is not seen again in the quarter, though their letters keep arriving.

regionalEffects: If the lord dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the rents fall last.

legendaryGroup.name: Nation Below
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the nation takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The roof settles. Each creature within 120 feet of the nation makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Bludgeoning damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

The air goes dead. Sound carries nowhere in the lair until the end of the nation's next turn; each creature within 60 feet of the nation makes a DC 21 Constitution saving throw or has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for that duration.

Firedamp seeps up. Each uncovered open flame within 120 feet of the nation is extinguished, and each creature within 10 feet of an extinguished flame makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Fire damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the nation's workings is altered in the following ways:

items: Nobody within 6 miles can say how deep the workings go. Every answer given is a different number, honestly meant.
Pit ponies and canaries will not go below the second level, and no handling moves them.
The owners' ledgers in this region show the same shift worked twice, in two different hands.

regionalEffects: If the nation dies, these effects end immediately, and the workings are found to have an ordinary floor.

legendaryGroup.name: Returned Room
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the room takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: Doors open in the air. Each creature within 60 feet of the room makes a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or is teleported to an unoccupied space the room can see within 30 feet of it.

The walls weep. A 20-foot-radius area the room can see within 60 feet is covered in clinging grave-clay until the end of the room's next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain, and a creature that starts its turn there takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Acid damage.

Every mirror in the lair shows an empty chair. Each creature within 60 feet of the room that can see a reflective surface makes a DC 20 Charisma saving throw, taking 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the room's cemetery is altered in the following ways:

items: Houses in the region are found with one room more than they were built with, always furnished and always cold.
Nothing buried here stays where it was put. Graves are found reopened from the inside, empty and tidy.
A family that moves away within 6 miles arrives at the new house to find their old parlor already in it.

regionalEffects: If the room dies, these effects end immediately, and the extra rooms are gone by morning.

legendaryGroup.name: Root-and-Rail Concord
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the concord takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The rails and the roots agree. A 40-foot-radius area the concord can see within 120 feet becomes a tangle of sleepers and root until the end of the concord's next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain, and a creature that starts its turn there makes a DC 24 Strength saving throw or has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its turn.

The watching face opens. Each creature within 60 feet of the concord that can see it makes a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the concord's next turn.

The hollow face calls. Each creature within 120 feet of the concord that has no conscious ally within 30 feet of it makes a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw, taking 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the concord's forest is altered in the following ways:

items: A railway runs through this forest that no company laid and no company can find to lift.
Travelers within 6 miles arrive at a station that is on no timetable, and are always the only passenger waiting.
Anyone who walks out of this forest alone walks out a day late and cannot account for the day.

regionalEffects: If the concord dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days, and the rails rust through within the year.

legendaryGroup.name: Unconfessed
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the unconfessed takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The veil passes over the square. Each creature within 60 feet of the unconfessed makes a DC 23 Charisma saving throw or has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of the unconfessed's next turn.

The ground gives at the knees. Each creature within 60 feet of the unconfessed that is within 10 feet of another creature makes a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw or has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

Doors stand open on rooms that should be private. Each creature within 90 feet of the unconfessed makes a DC 23 Wisdom saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save and half as much on a success. No player is required to disclose anything.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the unconfessed's parish is altered in the following ways:

items: No door within 6 miles stays shut. Latches lift, bolts draw, and nobody is ever found to have done it.
Written confessions in the parish copy themselves onto the next page in the same hand.
Everyone in the region knows one thing about a neighbor that they could not have learned, and none of them will say it.

regionalEffects: If the unconfessed dies, these effects end immediately, and the doors hold again from that night.

legendaryGroup.name: Wreck-Parish Confluence
lairActions: On Initiative Count 20 (losing Initiative ties), the confluence takes a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; it can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: Bells ring from under the water. Each creature within 120 feet of the confluence that can hear them makes a DC 24 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Thunder damage on a failed save and half as much on a success. A creature that fails also has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the end of the confluence's next turn.

The tide comes up through the floor. A 40-foot-radius area the confluence can see within 120 feet fills with knee-deep water until the end of the confluence's next turn. That area is Difficult Terrain for creatures other than the confluence.

The drowned surface. Three corpses rise in unoccupied spaces the confluence can see within 60 feet and float there until the end of the confluence's next turn. They are ordinary corpses, and a creature within 10 feet of one can be targeted by The Names Not Read.

regionalEffects: The country within 6 miles of the confluence's wreck is altered in the following ways:

items: Every church bell rings at the wrong hour, always two strokes short of the count, and no clapper can be removed that doesn't grow back by morning.
The sea returns nothing. Wreckage, cargo, and the drowned all stay down, and nets come up cut.
Mourners in the region can't finish a funeral. The words are forgotten at the graveside by everyone present at the same moment.

regionalEffects: If the confluence dies, these effects end immediately, and the coast gives up its dead over the following tide.

variantrule.name: How Maliced Lands Monsters Work
entries: Every monster in this collection was made by people feeling the same thing together for long enough. Fear, grief, rage, envy, longing, lust, joy, shame, and pride all do it, and none of them is special. Once made, a monster is real and independent: the feeling can fade and the monster stays. There is no ritual of calm and no reconciliation that unmakes one. They have to be destroyed by hand.
They want territory and subjects, not extermination. A monster keeps its people alive, inside its domain, and feeling, because that is the ground it grows in.

entries.name: Clan
entries: Monsters bred by the same landscape fight the same way, and each clan carries one shared trait that says how. A stat block's clan trait is always the first trait listed.

items: Tidebound (coast and sea). Strong in the water, badly weakened on dry ground.
Underleaf (deep forest). Fights from cover that can be burned or cleared.
Deepsign (mountains and mines). Reads the rock, and is blunted by an uncovered open flame.
Crowded Ground (walled cities). Strong against people standing close together, weak against people who spread out.
Anchored (urban haunts). Carries a physical object that is part of its body, with its own AC and Hit Points, that can be broken or covered.

entries: Fused monsters at the top of the range carry more than one clan's rules at once, in visibly separate organs.

entries.name: Trigger
entries: The emotion that made a monster decides whom it preys on. Each monster says so in plain words in its own traits; there is no table to look up.

items: Fear-born things key on Frightened creatures.
Grief-born things key on creatures below half their Hit Points and creatures near a corpse.
Rage-born things key on whoever has damaged them, and grow worse the more different people join in.
Envy-born things key on whoever has not been hurt yet.
Longing-born things key on creatures with no conscious ally within 30 feet.
Lust-born things key on Charmed creatures.
Joy-born things key on Prone creatures that can hear them.
Shame-born things key on Prone creatures with a witness nearby.
Pride-born things key on creatures that have just failed a saving throw against them, and are powerless against anyone who kneels.

entries.name: Counter
entries: Every monster here can be switched off, at least partly, by something the players can discover: a rule from its origin, a condition to end, an object to break, a formation to hold. The counter is printed in the stat block and repeated in the lore entry. Refusing a monster what feeds it is meant to be a real tactical resource, and the published Challenge Rating assumes the party finds the counter for roughly half the fight.
A monster's counter never requires a character to be immune to anything. If your players work out the rule, let it work.

entries.name: At the table
entries: This material is written for a mature table and its artwork is explicit. Nothing in any stat block requires a player to disclose a real secret, describe a real fear, reveal a character's private inventory, or roleplay a confession. Where a monster's origin touches those subjects, the mechanics are deliberately kept to conditions, damage, and position.
Challenge Ratings in this collection are design targets. They have not been verified at a table.
